text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- CFDT trade union leader Nicole Notat says in an interview she will only sign agreement of UNEDIC unemployment fund if early retirement measures are improved, calls for a 3,000-franc per month floor on unemployment benefits.
-- President Jacques Chirac in Tokyo for a four-day visit.

-- Details of planned merger of Air Inter Europe and Air France to be presented to the two airlines' workers at the end of this month, may include interim merger step along lines used for UTA airline in the past.
-- Press group Emap chairman France Kevin Hand calls in an interview for end to monopoly held by press distributor NMPP.
-- Aircraft engine maker SNECMA proceeds with buyout offer for Societe Europeenne de Propulsion.
-- 59 percent of small and medium-sized firm heads do not expect the economy to pick up in 1997, survey shows.
-- Non-farm payrolls shrank 0.1 percent in the third quarter, showing the first drop in three years.
-- Suez to sell four-billion-franc property loans portfolio to U.S. investment fund Whitehall through investment bank Goldman Sachs.
-- Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet confirms expectation of a return to profit for 1996, reaffirms desire to see Belgian businessman Albert Frere become one of the group's majority shareholder.
-- France considers cut in solidarity income tax targetting wealthy people, to avoid them leaving the country.
